rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects worshipped besides God are idols called gods, yet are owned, governed, and unable to bring benefit or harm.
rows.anchor: أي : تعبدونهم من دونه تعالى من الأصنام وتسمونهم آلهة

rows.speaker: الحدادي
rows.claim: Al-Haddadi says the idols are called servants because their makers fashioned them in human form.
rows.anchor: وقال الحدادي : سماها عبادا لأنهم صوروها على صورة الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is to call the idols for benefit or removal of harm; the command that they respond is a taunt meant to show their incapacity.
rows.anchor: في جلب نفع وكشف ضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim is that the idols can do what their worshippers cannot; the challenge exposes that claim as false.
rows.anchor: في زعمكم أنهم قادرون على ما أنتم عاجزون عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bodily response requires life, a mover, and moving and perceiving faculties; beings lacking all of these cannot act, and the walking predicate is the focus of the denial.
rows.anchor: إنما تتصور إذا كان لها محرك حياة وقوى محركة ومدركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording stresses walking with the legs because the negation turns on the asserted action, walking.
rows.anchor: ووصف الأرجل بالمشي بها للإيذان بأن مدار الإنكار هو الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disconnected am is understood as bal plus a hamza; batsh means taking something with force.
rows.anchor: أم منقطعة مقدرة ببل والهمزة والبطش الأخذ بقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether the idols have hands with which to seize what they want; bal shifts to a new mode of rebuke after the previous one is complete.
rows.anchor: بل للإضراب المفيد للانتقال من فن من التبكيت بعد تمامه إلى فن آخر منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walking comes first as the idols’ condition in themselves; grasping is their condition in relation to others.
rows.anchor: قدم المشي لأنه حالهم في أنفسهم والبطش حالهم بالنسبة إلى الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hands precede eyes to pair hands with legs; eyes precede ears because they are more familiar and more manifest in sight and effect.
rows.anchor: وأما تقديم الأعين فلما أنها أشهر من الآذان وأظهر عينا وأثرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters threatened the Prophet with harm from their gods; God challenges them and their idols to plot against him with all their power.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الكفار كانوا يخوفونه عليه السلام بآلهتهم قائلين نخاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tells them not to delay even an hour, confident that God will protect and guard him.
rows.anchor: فلا تمهلون ساعة فإني لا أبالي بكم لوثوقي على ولاية الله وحفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet voices fearless reliance on God as protector even if both worlds unite against the speaker.
rows.anchor: اكر هر دو جهانم خصم كردند نترسم ون نكهبا نم تو باشى

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi reports that Meccan unbelievers disliked prostration and asked whether they should prostrate to what Muhammad commanded, increasing in aversion.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (آورده اندكه كفار مكة تعظم ميكردند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those near their Lord are the angels, near by honor and rank rather than by distance or place.
rows.anchor: الملائكة المقربين لديه قرب الشرف والمكانة لاقرب المسافة والمكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels do not disdain worship but carry it out as commanded; their glorification declares God free of anything unworthy of His majesty.
rows.anchor: بل يؤدونها حسبما أمروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing lahu before the verb conveys exclusivity: they direct the utmost servitude and humility to God alone, without associating anything with Him.
rows.anchor: تقديم الجار على الفعل للحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ exclusive prostration indirectly reproaches other accountable beings; this is why prostration of recitation is prescribed at this verse.
rows.anchor: شيئا وهو تعريض بسائر المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration is the ultimate humility; it is prescribed in some places to remedy deficiency, as in forgetfulness prostration, and in others to oppose unbelievers and follow Muslims.
rows.anchor: السجدة نهاية الخضوع وإنما شرعت في موضع جبرا للنقصان كسجود السهو

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi counts twelve prostrations of recitation; Shafi‘i and Ahmad recognize one at the end of al-Hajj, while Imam Abu Hanifa does not.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (سجده تلاوت هارده موضع است در قرآن

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: For surah Sad, Abu Hanifa counts a recitation prostration because the Prophet prostrated there; the other imams do not, since the passage mentions bowing, not prostration.
rows.anchor: بمذهب امام أعظم هست لأن النبي عليه السلام قرأ سورة ص وسجد وبمذهب باقي ائمه نه

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali places the Fussilat prostration at the words إن كنتم إياه تعبدون; al-Shafi‘i follows this position.
rows.anchor: فعند علي رضي الله عنه هو قوله : {إن كنتم

rows.speaker: عمر وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Umar and Ibn Masud place the Fussilat prostration at لا يسأمون; Bursevi follows them as a precaution because delaying is permissible but doing it early is not.
rows.anchor: وعند عمر وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهما هو قوله : {لا يسامون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Abu Hanifa, prostration of recitation is immediately obligatory on reciter and listener, inside or outside prayer, and must be made up if missed; the other imams call it sunnah without make-up.
rows.anchor: ونزد امام أعظم سجده تلاوت برخواننده وشنونده درنماز وغير نماز واجبست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unnecessary delay is disliked; the seated worshipper should rise with takbir, recite the prayer’s glorification, prostrate with takbir, then sit, since this makes the prostration fuller.
rows.anchor: ويكره تأخير السجدة من غير ضرورة ويستحب أن يقوم القاعد فيكبر ويسبح تسبيح الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred glorification is سبحان ربي الأعلى three times; alternatives are خضعت للرحمن فاغفر لي يا رحمن and يا مقلب القلوب ثبت قلبي على دينك, favored by the author of al-Asrar al-Muhammadiyya.
rows.anchor: وهو الأصح وقيل يقول : "خضعت للرحمن فاغفر لي يا رحمن"

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet said in recitation prostration that his face prostrated to its Creator, who formed it and gave it hearing and sight by His power, then prayed for reward, pardon, provision, and acceptance.
rows.anchor: وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول في سجود التلاوة "سجد وجهي للذي خلقه

rows.speaker: ابن فخر الدين الرومي
rows.claim: Ibn Fakhr al-Din al-Rumi recommends distinct supplications for the prostrations in al-Isra, al-Araf or al-Sajda, and al-Najm, asking for praise, humility, and protection from pride.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فخر الدين الرومي إن قرأ سجدة سبحان ضم إليها ما ذكره سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persian verses shame the person who turns away from prostration and present obedience through prostration as the fitting path.
rows.anchor: توكنى از سجده او سر كشى به كه ازين شيوه قدم در كشى

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: The Shaykh al-Islam’s Persian maxim praises prostration and censures a head that is absent from it.
rows.anchor: وحشرت شيخ الإسلام قدس سره فرموده سرى كه دروسجودي نيست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet says the soul’s nobility comes through generosity and honor through prostration; lacking both makes one’s existence worse than nonexistence.
rows.anchor: شرف نفس بجودست وكرامت بسجود

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمة
rows.claim: The people near God have effaced their actions, traits, and selves in God’s commands, qualities, and essence; they no longer remain in themselves but through God.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمة" : {إن الذين عند ربك} يعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi continues Najmiyya’s account: because the saints effaced pride and their own actions, they do not disdain worship; in self-annihilation and abiding in God, their acts are worship rather than independent action.
rows.anchor: لأن الاستكبار من أخلاقهم وقد أفنوها في أخلاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is transcendent beyond indwelling, union, or fusion, and beyond claims that God is the servant or the servant God; He remains as He was in eternity.
rows.anchor: ينزهونه عن الحلول والاتصال والاتحاد وعن أن يكون هو العبد والعبد إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All beings bowed before God in pre-eternal nonexistence, submitting to His power to bring them into existence; in existence they surrender what they have to His decrees of annihilation, creation, and preservation.
rows.anchor: في الوجود والعدم من الأزل والأبد سجدوا له من الأزل في العدم منقادين مسخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi records the completion of al-Araf’s commentary in the first ten days of Safar 1101 AH and says al-Anfal follows.
rows.anchor: تمت سورة الأعراف بالرحم والراف مع ما يتعلق بها من التفسير والتأويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gloss identifies the hypocrites as three hundred men and one hundred seventy women.
rows.anchor: مردان منافق كه سيصد نفربودند)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Male and female hypocrites resemble one another in hypocrisy and distance from faith as parts of a single entity.
rows.anchor: أي متشابهون في النفاق والبعد عن الإيمان كأبعاض الشيء الواحد بالشخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They command disbelief and acts of disobedience.
rows.anchor: أي : بالكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prohibition of faith and obedience resumes and confirms the description and makes their opposition to the believers’ state explicit.
rows.anchor: أي : عن الإيمان والطاعة استئناف مقرر لمضمون ما سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Withholding the hands means refusing to spend in God’s cause, give charity, or do any good; it is a figure for stinginess.
rows.anchor: عن الإنفاق في سبيل الله وعن الصدقة وعن كل خير فإن قبض اليد كناية عن الشح

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi also interprets withholding their hands as not raising them in supplication and intimate prayer.
rows.anchor: أو عن رفعها للدعاء والمناجاة كما في "الكاشفي"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting God means neglecting His remembrance and abandoning His command; forgetting names its consequence, abandonment, because literal forgetfulness is not voluntary and is not blameworthy.
rows.anchor: صاروا غافلين عن ذكره وتركوا أمره حتى صار كالمنسي عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s forgetting means leaving them without His grace and favor, not overpowering or punishing them; literal forgetfulness is impossible for God.
rows.anchor: فتركهم من لطفه وفضله لا من قهره وتعذيبه وفسر النسيان أيضا بالمعنى المجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites are fully rebellious, departing from obedience and stripping away every good.
rows.anchor: الكاملون في التمرد والفسق الذي هو الخروج عن الطاعة والانسلاخ عن كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waʿd can announce a future benefit or harm; without specifying good or evil, waʿd and ʿidah denote promise, while īʿād and waʿīd denote threat.
rows.anchor: الوعد يستعمل في الخير بمعنى الإخبار بإيصال المنفعة قبل وقوعها وفي الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the unbelievers are those who openly manifest disbelief.
rows.anchor: أي : المجاهرين {نار جهنم} وهي من أسماء النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahannam may derive from the Arab word jahanam for a deep-bottomed well, reflecting the depth of Hell.
rows.anchor: تقول العرب للبئر البعيدة القعر جهنام فيجوز أن يكون جهنم مأخوذة من هذا اللفظ

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet heard a frightening sound; Gabriel explained that a stone had fallen from Hell’s rim for seventy years and had just reached its bottom, which God wanted him to hear.
rows.anchor: روي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سمع صوتا هاله فأتاه جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that their everlasting stay in Hell is decreed for them.
rows.anchor: أي مقدرا خلودهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet contrasts worldly sovereignty with the greater security of a poor person’s kingdom; the wise should reflect on worldly and afterlife conditions until death and burial.
rows.anchor: فقد تقرر حال أهل الدنيا وحال أهل الآخرة فالعاقل يعتبر ويتبصر إلى أن يموت ويقبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers share the true religion and monotheism, help each other in religious and worldly matters, and guide one another to higher degrees through spiritual training and purification.
rows.anchor: بعضهم على دين بعض في الحق ، أي متفقون في التوحيد وبعضهم معين بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They enjoin every good, including faith and obedience, and encourage one another to seek God, the real good, as expressed in the saying I loved to be known.
rows.anchor: جنس المعروف الشامل لكل خير ومنه الإيمان والطاعة ويهيج بعضهم بعضا في طلب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They forbid every evil, including disbelief and sins that sever a person from God in this world and beyond.
rows.anchor: جنس المنكر المنتظم لكل شر ومنه الكفر والمعاصي التي تقطع العبد عن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer means constant remembrance and vigilant, present hearts that trade cannot distract; these are people of unveiling and hearts, opposite to those who forgot God.
rows.anchor: فلا يزالون يذكرون الله تعالى ويديمون مراقبة القلب وحضوره مع الله بحيث لا تلهيهم تجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike hypocrites who withhold their hands, they pay obligatory zakat and give any surplus beyond necessary sufficiency, purifying themselves of worldly attachment.
rows.anchor: فهم يؤدون الزكاة الواجبة بل ينفقون ما فضل عن كفافهم الضروري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They obey every command and prohibition, in contrast to hypocrites described by complete rebellion and departure from obedience.
rows.anchor: في كل أمر ونهي وهو بمقابلة وصف المنافقين بكمال الفسق والخروج عن الطاعة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Najmiyya reads the qualities as sincerity: hypocrites may pray and give zakat outwardly, yet follow ego and desire for worldly interests instead of obeying God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى الإخلاص في معاملتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will pour out mercy through support and victory, save them from Hell’s punishment and the pain of distance from Him, and admit them to Paradise and nearness.
rows.anchor: يفيض عليهم آثار رحمته من التأييد والنصرة البتة وينجيهم من العذاب الأليم

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الإشارة
rows.claim: Some people of inward interpretation describe mercy at five trials: death, the grave, receiving the record, the balance, and standing before God, easing each hardship and protecting the believer.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض أهل الإشارة. {سيرحمهم الله} في خمسة مواضع عند الموت وسكراته

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A hadith associates the five daily prayers with ease at death, in the grave, at Munkar and Nakir’s questioning, at the balance, and on the narrow bridge; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من صلى صلاة الفجر هان عليه الموت وغصته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s might explains His promise: He can honor His allies, subdue His enemies, and bestow favor on those who obey Him.
rows.anchor: تعليل الوعد ، أي : قوي قادر على إعزاز أوليائه

words: وَمَا لَهُمْ فِي ٱلْأَرْضِ مِن وَلِيٍّ وَلَا نَصِيرٍ
rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Najmiyya says that when a perfect shaykh rejects someone from spiritual allegiance, even a world full of saints cannot rescue him from rejection unless God wills, despite his attachment to their guidance.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن من ابتلي برد ولاية شيخ كامل ولو امتلأت الأرض بالمشايخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A covenant here is a pact and an oath.
rows.anchor: المعاهدة المعاقدة واليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lantasaddaqanna derives from lantasaddaqanna, with ta assimilated into sad; it means giving zakat and other charity.
rows.anchor: وأصله لنتصدقن أدغمت التاء في الصاد والمتصدق معطي الصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term sadaqa signals the servant’s truthfulness in servitude.
rows.anchor: وسميت صدقة لدلالتها على صدق العبد في العبودية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the promised righteous deed was pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما يريد الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account identifies the covenant-breaker as Thalaba ibn Hatib al-Ansari, a constant mosque-goer nicknamed the mosque’s dove, whose forehead bore marks of frequent prostration.
rows.anchor: نزلت في ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري كان ملازما مسجد رسول الله ليلا ونهارا

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Thalaba explained that he and his wife shared one garment for prayer; the Prophet warned that a little wealth one can thank for is better than much one cannot bear.
rows.anchor: فقال له عليه السلام يوما "ما لك صرت تعمل عمل المنافقين بتعجيل الخروج"

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet asked Thalaba whether he would be content like a prophet, saying mountains could become gold and silver at his wish, but worldly wealth can deceive the unwise.
rows.anchor: فراجعه فقال عليه السلام "أما ترضى أن تكون مثل نبي الله

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: After Thalaba swore to pay everyone’s due, the Prophet prayed three times for him to receive wealth.
rows.anchor: فراجعه وقال يا رسول الله والذي بعثك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thalaba’s sheep multiplied until he left the mosque, first missing congregational prayer except noon and afternoon, then missing all congregation and Friday prayer as he moved farther away.
rows.anchor: فاتخذ غنما فنمت كما ينمو الدود حتى ضاقت بها أزقة المدينة

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: When told Thalaba’s wealth filled valleys, the Prophet twice lamented him; after 9:103, collectors brought the required alms schedule, but Thalaba called it a tax and refused.
rows.anchor: فلما نزل قوله تعالى : {خذ من أموالهم صدقة} (التوبة : 103) استعمل النبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After God gave them wealth from His bounty, they withheld its due, abandoned obedience and their covenant, and remained habitual turnaways.
rows.anchor: أي : منعوا حق الله منه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When the collectors returned, the Prophet said woe to Thalaba twice before they told him what had happened; Umar then warned Thalaba that revelation had condemned him.
rows.anchor: فلما رجعا قال لهما رسول الله قبل أن يكلماه "يا ويح ثعلبة" مرتين

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Thalaba brought the alms, but the Prophet refused it because God had forbidden acceptance; the Prophet called this the recompense for Thalaba’s refusal and calling it a tax.
rows.anchor: فجاء ثعلبة بالصدقة فقال عليه السلام : "إن الله منعني أن أقبل منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thalaba’s distress over rejection was attributed to public shame, not repentance from hypocrisy; Abu Bakr and Umar also refused his later payments, and he died under Uthman.
rows.anchor: لا لأنه تاب عن النفاق بل للحوق العار من عدم قبول زكاته مع المسلمين

rows.speaker: الحدادي
rows.claim: Al-Haddadi states that Uthman did not accept Thalaba’s charity.
rows.anchor: قال الحدادي : لم يقبل منه عثمان صدقته انتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s punishment followed their breach of the promise to give charity and be righteous, and their continuing lies in all statements, including that promise.
rows.anchor: بسبب إخلافهم ما وعدوه من التصدق والصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is confirmatory: the covenant-makers did know that God knows their secrets and private conversations.
rows.anchor: أي : من عاهدوا الله والاستفهام للتقرير ، أي قد علموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their hidden resolve to break the promise and their private talk, including calling zakat a tax and other speech devoid of good, whether said secretly or publicly.
rows.anchor: ما أسروه في أنفسهم من العزم على الإخلاف ولم يتكلموا به سرا ولا جهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najwa means conferring a secret; the verb najāhu or nājāhu means speaking privately, and najwa is a secret or confidential speech.
rows.anchor: والتناجي (بايكديكر راز كردن) يقال نجاه نجوى وناجاه مناجاة ساره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet warns against contemplating disobedience when one knows God knows and sees.
rows.anchor: مكن انديشه عصيان وميدانى كه ميداند مبين در روى اين وآن وميدانى كه مى بيند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A vow of devotional giving, such as promising half of a thousand dirhams if granted, must be fulfilled; a vow of a non-devotional act or sin incurs expiation if broken.
rows.anchor: من نذر نذرا فيه قربة نحو أن يقول إن رزقني الله ألف درهم فعلي أن تصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a broken oath-like vow, expiation is freeing a slave, feeding ten poor people, or clothing them, with the person choosing one; inability requires three consecutive fasting days.
rows.anchor: فالواجب واحد من هذه الثلاثة والعبد مخير فيه فإن عجز عن أحد هذه الأشياء الثلاثة صام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A vow conditioned on an event the person hopes will occur, such as a return, recovery, debt payment, or acquiring a servant, must be fulfilled because its wording is a vow, not an oath.
rows.anchor: وإن علق النذر بشرط يريد وجوده ، نحو أن يقول : إن قدم فلان أو إن قدمت من سفري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a vow is conditioned on an event the person hopes will not occur, such as speaking to someone, breaking it is discharged by oath expiation.
rows.anchor: وإن علقه بشرط لا يريد وجوده ، كقوله : إن كلمت فلانا أو دخلت الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A vowed act whose kind has a basis in obligatory worship—fasting, prayer, charity, or retreat—is binding; acts with no obligatory counterpart, such as visiting the sick or building a bridge, are not.
rows.anchor: والمنذور إذا كان له أصل في الفروض أي واجب من جنسه لزم الناذر كالصوم والصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The principle is that a person’s self-imposed obligation is validated by God’s obligation so that the benefit attached to the vow is realized.
rows.anchor: والأصل فيه أن إيجاب العبد معتبر بإيجاب الله تعالى تحصيلا للمصلحة المعلقة بالنذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unconditional vow is not restricted to a time, place, amount, or recipient; unlike Zafar, the Hanafi view accepts substituting another day, dirham, and poor person for the specified ones.
rows.anchor: والنذر الغير المعلق لا يختض بزمان ومكان ودرهم وفقير بخلاف المعلق

rows.speaker: زفر
rows.claim: Zafar holds that a vow specifying this day, this dirham, and this poor recipient is not discharged by giving another dirham on another day to someone else.
rows.anchor: ولا يجزئه عند زفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wise should work through the rulings of sacred law and the manners of the spiritual path until wholly free of hypocrisy; admitting sin is a believer’s inheritance from Adam.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يجتهد بأحكام الشريعة وآداب الطريقة إلى أن يحصل الخلاص من النفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Adam wept over his sin for two hundred years until God accepted his repentance and forgave him; penitents should therefore weep and humble themselves often.
rows.anchor: روي أنه بكى على ذنبه مائتي سنة حتى قبل الله توبته وغفر ذنبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A penitent should send blessings on the Prophet, intercessor for prophets and saints; Adam sought God through Muhammad’s standing, and believers should ask forgiveness for all believing men and women.
rows.anchor: ويصلي على النبي عليه السلام فإنه شفيع لكل نبي وولي ولذا توسل به آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness is the servant’s request that God pardon sins; God’s forgiveness means concealing them by grace rather than exposing or shaming the sinner.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الاستغفار سؤال العبد ربه أن يغفر له ذنوبه ومعنى مغفرته لذنوب عباده أن يسترها عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A condition of repentance is not to commit sin deliberately; what occurs through forgetfulness or error is pardoned by God’s grace.
rows.anchor: ومن شرط التوبة أن لا يتعمد ذنبا فإن وقع منه بسهو أو خطأ فهو معفو عنه

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafiz’s Persian couplet argues that since sin struck the pure Adam, people cannot credibly claim to be sinless.
rows.anchor: قال الحافظ : جايى كه برق عصيان بر آدم صفى زد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to Muhammad concerns taking charity from the wealth of those who stayed behind and admitted their sins.
rows.anchor: {خذ} يا محمد {من أموالهم} أي : من أموال هؤلاء المتخلفين المعترفين بذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sadaqa is construed as a circumstantial accusative: take from their wealth in the state of giving charity.
rows.anchor: {صدقة} حال كونك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charity cleanses them of the stain of having stayed behind.
rows.anchor: {تطهرهم} أي : عما تلطخوا به من أوضار التخلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through the charity and its collection, their good deeds grow and they rise to the ranks of the sincere.
rows.anchor: تنمى بتلك الصدقة وأخذها حسناتهم وترفعهم إلى مراتب المخلصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After their repentance and release from bonds, the wrongdoers brought all their wealth and asked the Prophet to give charity for them; he disliked it, then the verse came and he took a third as completion of repentance and expiation for staying behind.
rows.anchor: روي أنه لما حلهم النبي عليه السلام من وثاقهم وتاب الله عليهم راحوا إلى منازلهم وجاؤوا بأموالهم كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first account this charity is not obligatory zakat, which is not collected in this manner.
rows.anchor: فهذه الصدقة ليست الصدقة المفروضة فإنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats the passage as a new command requiring zakat from affluent Muslims even without a previously mentioned group; most jurists hold this, and sadaqa signals truthful servitude.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هذا كلام مبتدأ نزل لإيجاب أخذ الزكاة من الأغنياء عليه

rows.speaker: الاختيار
rows.claim: Al-Ikhtiyar says the imam forcibly collects zakat from a refuser and places it where due, citing this verse.
rows.anchor: قال في "الاختيار" : من امتنع عن أداء الزكاة أخذها الإمام كرها

rows.speaker: الأشباه
rows.claim: Al-Ashbah reports that the relied-upon school position is not to seize zakat by force.
rows.anchor: وفي "الأشباه" المعتمد في المذهب عدم الأخذ كرها

rows.speaker: المحيط
rows.claim: Al-Muhit says an official should not forcibly take zakat; if taken without consent it does not discharge the duty, so the payer is compelled by imprisonment to pay personally.
rows.anchor: قال في "المحيط" : ومن امتنع من أداء الزكاة فالساعي لا يأخذ منه كرها

rows.speaker: المبسوط
rows.claim: Al-Mabsut’s sounder view is that payments to unjust officials of charity, tithes, jizya, kharaj, levies, or confiscations discharge the owner’s obligation if paid with charitable intent; another view advises repeating payment if the collector knew its nature.
rows.anchor: قال في "المبسوط" : وما يأخذ ظلمة زماننا من الصدقات والعشور والجزية والخراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to pray for their good and blessing and ask forgiveness for them.
rows.anchor: أي ادع لهم بالخير والبركة واستغفر لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s prayers calm their souls and reassure their hearts; sakan is a passive-form noun, like naqd meaning something spent or broken.
rows.anchor: تسكن إليها نفوسهم وتطمئن بها قلوبهم فهو فعل بمعنى مفعول كالنقض بمعنى المنقوض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears their confession and knows their remorse.
rows.anchor: {والله سميع} باعترافهم {عليم} بندامتهم

rows.speaker: الكافي
rows.claim: Al-Kafi cites this verse and the report pray over every righteous and sinful person as evidence that funeral prayer is prescribed.
rows.anchor: قال في "الكافي" : الصلاة على الميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Adam was shrouded and embalmed with materials from Paradise, washed and shrouded by angels, and prayed over by an angel leading the angels.
rows.anchor: روي أن آدم عليه السلام لما توفي أتي بحنوط وكفن من الجنة ونزلت الملائكة

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: In another account, Seth asks Gabriel to pray over Adam; Gabriel tells Seth to lead, and Seth prays with thirty takbirs before the burial and lahd.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية : قال ولده شيث لجبريل عليه السلام صل عليه فقال له جبريل تقدم أنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Adam accounts make washing, shrouding, funeral prayer, burial, and lahd ancient religious practices.
rows.anchor: ومنه يعلم أن الغسل والتكفين والصلاة والدفن واللحد من الشرائع القديمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that funeral prayer is unique to this community does not contradict ancient precedent: Quraysh need not have known of it, or they would have practiced it.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم صلاة الجنازة من خصائص هذه الأمة ولا منافاة لأنه لا يلزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say pre-Islamic Arabs washed and shrouded their dead, then the deceased’s guardian stood by the bier, recited virtues, invoked mercy, and buried the body.
rows.anchor: وفي كلام بعضهم كانوا في الجاهلية يغسلون موتاهم وكانوا يكفنونهم ويصلون عليهم

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: When the Prophet reached Medina, Bara ibn Marur had died; the Prophet and companions prayed at his grave with four takbirs. Scholars date the obligation to the first Hijri year.
rows.anchor: روي أن النبي عليه السلام لما قدم المدينة وجد البراء بن معرور رضي الله عنه قد مات

rows.speaker: القنية
rows.claim: Al-Qunya states that someone who denies the obligatory status of funeral prayer is an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: ومن أنكر فرضية صلاة الجنازة كفر كما في "القنية".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Washing the dead is a communal obligation; intention is not required for the washing’s validity but does discharge the duty for the washer and community, and if everyone omits it all are sinful.
rows.anchor: إن غسل الميت فرض كفاية فإذا تركوا أثموا فبنية الغسل يسقط الفرض عن ذمة الغاسل وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead become impure at death like other blood-bearing animals, but washing purifies them as an honor; even a body found in water must be washed because people have not performed the commanded act.
rows.anchor: وإنما يغسل الميت لأنه يتنجس بالموت كسائر الحيوانات الدموية إلا أنه يطهر بالغسل
